principles.title:
Made to fit your editor.
Not replace it.
principles.description: Use your existing shortcuts, language extensions, and compiler. ACStride brings the contest context; VS Code stays your workspace.
principles.local: Your solutions stay on your machine.
principles.localBody: No ACStride account is needed for the current local workflow.
principles.honestBody: This is an early preview. Downloads may encounter site verification; keep the official site available.

items.a: No. ACStride is a desktop VS Code extension, currently named CFIDE inside the extension. It adds contest tools to the editor you already use.

items.q: Do I need to install Python?
items.a: Only to run your Python solutions. Public problem downloads use a private bundled runtime. C++ solutions require your own compiler.

items.q: Can it submit directly to Codeforces?
items.a: Not currently. It saves and copies the selected solution and opens the matching official submission page. You paste and submit there.
Saved code, custom tests, and cached statements remain available. Downloads, rankings, and public submissions require a network connection.

download.title:

download.intro: The extension is in early preview. Marketplace publication and public prebuilt downloads are not available yet. Build a platform-specific VSIX from the source to try it today.
download.sourceNote: Source is visible; no open-source license has been selected for the extension.
download.requirementsBody: Desktop VS Code, a trusted local folder, and a C++ compiler and/or Python 3 for your solutions. The downloader needs no separate Python installation.
download.platformNote: Targets do not imply published or validated binaries. Check the repository's CI and packaging instructions before distributing a build.
steps: Build the VSIX using the repository's development and packaging instructions.
In VS Code, open Extensions: Install from VSIX… and choose the matching package.
Open a trusted folder, add a contest, and check your C++ / Python environment in Settings.
download.warning: Local programs run on your computer, not in a security sandbox. Use only code you trust.

docs.eyebrow: A SHORT PATH TO YOUR FIRST RUN
docs.title: The quick start.
docs.intro: From a fresh installation to a tested solution, without the detour.

sections.title: 01 / Set up your environment
sections.body: Install a matching VSIX. Open a trusted local folder, then open CFIDE Settings from the sidebar gear. Configure your C++ compiler and/or Python interpreter and select Check all. A green tick means that check passed.

sections.title: 02 / Add a contest
sections.body: Use the sidebar + button and paste a regular Codeforces contest URL or ID. Upcoming contests download released problems while VS Code is running. Adding a contest does not register you for the official round.

sections.title: 03 / Read and write
sections.body: Choose A, B, or another problem. Read the statement on the left and use the native code editor on the right. Switch languages with the language control; each language keeps its own file.

sections.title: 04 / Run your cases
sections.body: Use sample tabs or add a custom case with +. Run all saves the selected solution before testing. Compare expected and actual output; local AC is not an official verdict.

sections.title: 05 / Submit on Codeforces
sections.body: Use Copy code & open submission page. It saves and copies the selected language's solution. Paste it on Codeforces, choose the correct compiler, and submit there. Set your public handle to track submissions and rankings.

sections.title: 06 / Make it yours
sections.body: Choose an interface language, configure starter code for C++ and Python, and adjust tools in Settings. Per-contest download and archive controls live in that contest's settings.

docs.troubleBody: Retry the problem download later. Site verification may block anonymous requests. Existing solutions, custom cases, and cached statements are preserved. Keep the official website as your fallback.

privacy.title: Privacy & licensing.
privacy.intro: This page describes the current early-preview website and extension. It is not a promise about services that have not launched.

sections.title: This website
sections.body: This version has no ACStride sign-in, payment form, analytics SDK, or advertising tracker. Your language is reflected in the URL. The hosting provider may process requests and operational logs under its own policies.

sections.title: The extension
sections.body: The current local workflow does not require an ACStride account or upload your solutions to an ACStride service. Public requests are sent to Codeforces. The copy-and-open action puts code on your system clipboard; you choose whether to paste and submit it.

sections.title: External services
sections.body: Links to GitHub, Codeforces, and other services leave this website. Those services apply their own privacy practices and terms. Website hosting is separate from the local extension.

sections.title: Licensing
sections.body: The extension has not selected an open-source license; do not assume permission for commercial reuse. The CF Tool development fork retains its upstream MIT license. This website's original code and content are all rights reserved, except for third-party components under their own licenses.

sections.title: Questions
sections.body: For product or privacy questions, open an issue in the extension repository. Do not include passwords, cookies, source code you want to keep private, or other sensitive information in a public issue.
